title: Power Rename error in context menu.

judgment.rationale: The report includes concrete context-menu settings, trigger, expected appearance, two screenshots, and a diagnostic ZIP. The remaining uncertainty is whether Explorer's native menu renderer or PowerRename's inserted command path causes the transparent frame.
evidence: The reporter describes PowerToys 0.101.2362 from Microsoft Store, with standard and extended context menus enabled, and right-clicking in Explorer.
Two screenshots show the reported context-menu border/width appearance.
The attached PowerToysReport ZIP was summarized by the automated triage comment as Windows 11 build 22000 with no crash/error signature; that summary says the issue looks like context-menu rendering.
The bot asked for repro steps, but the issue body already supplies the menu setting and triggering interaction.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce the reported visual defect on the cited Windows build and compare the legacy and extended Explorer menu paths before proposing a PowerRename workaround.

fix_assessment.rationale: A PowerRename-specific trigger is possible because its shell extension contributes a menu item, but Explorer paints the native menu and the issue does not establish which menu implementation produces the defect.

proposed_fixes.title: Isolate the PowerRename context-menu rendering trigger
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The PowerRename shell extension contributes a caption and optional icon to Explorer's native context menu; a menu-width or rendering interaction may expose an Explorer frame-paint defect, but no application-owned border drawing is evident.
plan: Reproduce on the reported Windows 11 build with both standard and extended context-menu settings, recording whether the defect appears in each menu surface and for blank-area versus selected-item menus.
Compare the legacy QueryContextMenu insertion with the IExplorerCommand title/icon path and determine whether the contributed item or its caption changes the native menu geometry.

If the PowerRename item is shown to trigger the defect, test the smallest shell-compatible insertion or caption workaround; otherwise route the rendering defect to the Windows shell owner rather than changing unrelated PowerRename code.
verification: On Windows 11 build 22000 with PowerToys 0.101.2362, reproduce the context-menu appearance with the reported settings and compare it with the same Explorer menu without the PowerRename entry.
Repeat on a current Windows 11 build to establish whether the behavior is limited to the reported shell version.

confidence.rationale: The visual report is concrete, but PowerRename supplies menu metadata rather than drawing the Explorer frame; a PowerToys-specific workaround is unproven.

issue_context.summary: PowerRename's context-menu entry is reported beside a transparent/invisible right border when the standard and extended menu option is enabled; the report includes screenshots and a diagnostic archive.
known_information: The report identifies PowerToys 0.101.2362 from Microsoft Store and the standard-and-extended context-menu setting.
The issue includes two screenshots and a PowerToys diagnostic ZIP.
The automated triage comment reports Windows 11 build 22000 and no crash/error signatures in its sanitized diagnostic subset.
The issue's bot comment requests repro detail even though the body already specifies the setting and Explorer interaction.
inferences: The native Explorer menu renderer likely owns the frame painting, while the PowerRename item may affect the menu width or layout.
A related 2024 issue #31280 discusses PowerRename context-menu rendering but does not establish that its high-DPI/context-menu symptoms are the same transparent-border defect.
issue_context.analysis: The existing report is reproducible enough for a maintainer to test without asking for another ZIP or generic steps. Source inspection shows PowerRename inserts a menu item/title and optional icon; it does not draw the Explorer menu border. The first discriminator is whether the issue follows the PowerRename item across the two shell menu paths and Windows builds.
initial_investigation: Inspected src/modules/powerrename/dll/PowerRenameExt.cpp: CPowerRenameMenu::QueryContextMenu inserts the command string and optional bitmap; IExplorerCommand::GetTitle and GetIcon return menu metadata.
No PowerRename-owned context-menu frame/border painting path was found in the inspected shell extension.
Issue #31280 is still open but is a broad, older context-menu report; the available evidence does not justify classifying this report as a duplicate.
The Needs-Author-Feedback label is not treated as proof that new reporter information is required because the issue body already contains the repro sequence.

related_issues.relationship: Older broad PowerRename context-menu report; no matching transparent-border symptom established.

actions.label: Reproduce transparent Explorer menu border
actions.note: Screenshots, diagnostics, and the menu configuration are already present; verify locally before asking the reporter for more evidence.

reproduce.title: Compare PowerRename shell menu rendering
reproduce.version_requirement: PowerToys 0.101.2362; Windows 11 build 22000 as reported, then compare a current Windows 11 build
prerequisites: Explorer with PowerRename enabled and its standard-and-extended context-menu option active.
Use a selected renamable item for the command-insertion path; separately test right-click on empty Explorer space as described in the report.
steps: Open the Explorer context menu using the reported setting and capture the right border when the PowerRename entry is present.
Compare the standard and extended menu surfaces and note where the PowerRename item appears.
Repeat without the PowerRename entry, then repeat on a current Windows 11 build.
Determine whether the border defect follows the PowerRename item or the Explorer menu surface independently of it.
reproduce.expected_result: Explorer renders an opaque, complete context-menu border with and without the PowerRename entry.
reproduce.actual_to_confirm: Whether adding the PowerRename command changes menu width/layout and triggers the transparent border, and whether the result depends on the shell build.

status.label: Reproduce Explorer menu rendering
status.detail: Repro evidence is present; maintainer comparison must identify whether PowerRename or Explorer owns the rendering defect.

next_action.label: Reproduce Explorer menu rendering
next_action.reason: Establish the shell path and Windows-build dependency before approving a PowerRename change.
